── Step 2 of 28 · Role types ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Site-wide objects (role types, groups, statuses, resolutions, priorities, issue link types, issue
  types and custom fields) are shared by every space on the site, so existing ones are compared,
  never changed. Missing ones with mode ensure are created; missing ones with mode reuse must be
  created first.

  ✓ exists   Administrators  matches (id 10002)
  + create   Triage Team     new role type · site-wide

── Step 11 of 28 · Screens ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Screens and workflows can be used by several spaces. A managed one (mode managed, the default) is
  created for this space when missing, and changed to match the spec only while this space alone
  uses it; a change that removes something needs --allow-delete. A reused one must exist, and is
  never changed.

  + create   VULN Triage Screen  new screen · 1 tab, 2 fields
                                   POST /rest/api/3/screens
                                   PUT /rest/api/3/screens/{screenId}/tabs/{tabId} (names the first tab)
                                   POST /rest/api/3/screens/{screenId}/tabs/{tabId}/fields × 2
  ✗ differs  Default Screen      exists (id 1) but does not match the spec:
                                   tab "Field Tab" fields
                                     spec: Summary, Description
                                     Jira: Summary
                                 Fix: Change tab "Field Tab" fields in the spec to match Jira. A
                                 reused screen is used as it is and never changed.
  ✗ error    VULN Old Screen     exists (id 10100), but this tool did not create it (its description
                                 has no [managed-by] marker)

── Step 17 of 28 · Permissions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Who may do what in the space, who is told of changes, who may see which work items, and which
  priorities it offers are schemes too, decided the same way: the space's scheme is kept when it
  matches; otherwise the one the spec's binding names, or a new one named after
  space.managed_prefix, is used, and step 25 switches the space to it. A switch that would leave
  work items without their priority or security level is blocked.

  ■ blocked  Permission scheme  new permission scheme "VULN Permission Scheme" · 1 permission; step
                                25 switches the space to it from "Default software scheme"; but it
                                grants Administer projects to nobody
                                Fix: Grant ADMINISTER_PROJECTS to someone (role:Administrators, for
                                example), or nobody could administer the space.
                                  POST /rest/api/3/permissionscheme
                                  DELETE /rest/api/3/permissionscheme/{schemeId}/permission/{permissionId} (grants Jira adds)

── Step 25 of 28 · Scheme switches ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  The space is switched to the schemes the steps above decided on, one kind at a time. A switch is
  blocked while it would affect work items: their count is shown, with what to do first.

  ✓ exists   Schemes  the space keeps every scheme it uses
